video.title: A Business Anyone Can Start Today With Just $100

summary: Chris Koerner presents mailbox installation and repair as a little-known local service opportunity, with examples of custom mailbox sellers and HOA contracts. He outlines three approaches: hands-on repairs and standard installs, distinctive mailboxes sold online, and larger HOA jobs. He recommends checking local demand before buying tools, then using neighbourhood marketing, photos, and referrals to win early work. The video mixes operator anecdotes, host estimates, and hypothetical market calculations, so its financial figures are claims rather than verified results.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Solo presenter of The Koerner Office.

ideas.name: Local mailbox repair and standard installation
ideas.one_liner: Repair, replace, or install standard residential mailboxes as a hands-on neighbourhood service.
ideas.business_model: Per-job fees for repair, replacement, or installation.
ideas.customer: Homeowners with broken, leaning, rusty, faded, or outdated mailboxes.
ideas.problem: Mailboxes deteriorate or get damaged, and homeowners may lack the tools or know-how to fix them.
ideas.offer: Inspect and repair mailboxes, or install a standard mailbox using a post, concrete, mailbox, and screws. The host also describes masonry mailboxes as a premium option.

pricing.model: Per job; the host suggests introductory pricing to build reviews and later charging more.

price_points.label: Example price when materials cost about $100

pricing.notes: The transcript also gives a garbled hourly earnings estimate, 'between $1 and $200 per hour'; it is not clear enough to use as a reliable rate.

acquisition_channels.details: Walk streets, note damaged mailboxes, then knock on the doors of those homes. The host suggests doing this during the initial neighbourhood audit.

quote.text: If you really want to have a bias for action, go ahead and just knock on the door right then.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Use flyers, postcards, or door hangers targeted to homes with visibly damaged mailboxes; the host suggests timing mail after major storms and using before-and-after photos.

quote.text: When you send the direct mail after these storms, your dollar goes so much further.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Join neighbourhood Facebook groups, provide value, share completed work, and reply quickly when someone asks for help. The host recounts an HOA job originating from a reply to a Facebook post.

quote.text: That came from one Facebook reply. Not his original post, just a reply to another post that he saw.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: The host names Facebook Marketplace as a customer acquisition option.
Create and optimize a Google Business Profile with photos, videos, FAQs, and hours to attract local leads.

quote.text: When we're talking about any home service or any local business, Google business profile is a nonnegotiable.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Target Facebook or Nextdoor ads to older neighbourhoods with visibly worn mailboxes; test different advertising angles.

quote.text: You can run nextdoor ads to specific neighborhoods.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Ask realtors, handymen, and landscapers to refer mailbox jobs in exchange for a referral fee.

quote.text: Every time you see a home that needs a mailbox, send them to me and I'll give you a referral fee.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Use bandit signs near completed jobs, or place flyers in bags with rocks on targeted driveways. Do not put flyers inside mailboxes.

quote.text: The more visual an outdoor home service, the more effective bandit signs are.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Build referral relationships with realtors, local handymen, and landscapers who encounter homes needing mailbox work.

ideas.delivery: The owner does the physical inspection, digging, post setting, assembly, repair, painting, and cleanup. The host says a motorized auger can make a job faster; masonry work takes more skill.
unit_economics_claims: The host estimates about $100 for standard materials and a suggested standard installation price of $350–$550.
The host says a standard installation takes about 1–2 hours and that 5–6 may be completed in a day.
A Reddit commenter reported charging $9,000 to repair, straighten, and paint 23 mailbox stands in about a week.
ideas.startup_cost: The host says the basic approach can start with $1–$500; he estimates materials for a standard installation at about $100.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: The host recommends auditing and selling immediately, but gives no measured time to first revenue.

acquisition.how: An agent could help identify neighbourhoods and draft ads, but door knocking, local networking, and much of the group engagement require a person. UK cold outreach must follow PECR and calling-screening rules.

onboarding.how: A form could collect address, photos, and job details, while a person confirms access, condition, and scope.

delivery.how: Digging, installing, repairing, and painting are physical tasks that require a person on site.

billing.how: An agent could prepare quotes and invoices and trigger payment reminders, with human review of job scope and final charges.

support.how: Software could answer routine questions and schedule visits, but a person would handle damage complaints, site issues, and rework.

uk_applicability.notes: Mailbox repair and installation is a familiar home service in the UK. Adapt pricing, materials, permissions, and local marketing to UK conditions.

risks: Physical work limits how much an agent-run business can automate.
The host says jobs may require insurance, upset customers may need attention, and some work may have to be redone for free.
The host says not to put flyers inside mailboxes; his legal example is about the US, so check UK postal and advertising rules before distributing material.
Homeowners may prefer DIY or already have a handyman; validate willingness to pay before buying tools.
In the UK, unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals and sole traders is restricted by PECR; cold calls need TPS/CTPS screening.

tactics.name: Audit a neighbourhood before spending
steps: Walk or drive through neighbourhoods and record the types of mailbox damage you see.
Write down exact addresses and look for at least 20 opportunities within a 15-minute drive.
Talk to homeowners and try to sell the work while the need is visible.
Do not buy tools until a first job is secured.

quote.text: You're not just doing research. You're going to sell to these people.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use early jobs to create proof
steps: Do your own mailbox first if needed and photograph the process.
Take before-and-after photos and videos of every paid job.
Use early jobs to gather reviews and build a portfolio.
Store job photos in Google Drive for future promotional material.

quote.text: Do it for yourself first just to document the process and to be your own case study.
quote.speaker: Reddit commenter

tactics.name: Start with an accessible price, then raise it with evidence
steps: Quote early jobs below the rate you eventually want while building case studies and reviews.
Track actual materials and labour so later prices reflect real job costs.
Raise prices after you have photos and customer proof.

quote.text: you just want to get some case studies. You want to get some fivestar reviews. You want to get some traction.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Get discovered inside neighbourhood groups
steps: Join relevant neighbourhood Facebook groups and Nextdoor.
Watch for posts asking for help and reply quickly with a useful answer.
Share work and helpful information before making direct promotional posts.
Use before-and-after pictures to show the result.

quote.text: We're talking about you kind of lurking in the shadows, waiting for someone else to post so you can jump on it as soon as possible.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Test targeted local advertising
steps: Select older neighbourhoods where damaged mailboxes are common.
Run Facebook or Nextdoor ads only in those areas.
Test 10–20 marketing angles and keep the ones that perform best.
Time direct mail after major snow or wind storms and include before-and-after photos.

quote.text: I guarantee you if you test like 10 to 20 marketing angles, you're going to find one or two that command all of your time because they work so well.

tactics.name: Build referral routes through adjacent trades
steps: Ask handymen whether they take mailbox jobs and offer to pay for referrals.
Approach landscapers who visit many homes and ask them to refer visibly damaged mailboxes.
Build relationships with realtors who advise sellers on home improvements.

quote.text: I call this piggybacking.

tactics.name: Keep the business name broad enough to allow expansion
steps: Start in the mailbox niche, but avoid a name that prevents customers from understanding adjacent services.
Add related services such as pressure washing or exterior painting only if mailbox demand is too small for the target business size.

quote.text: Don't pigeon hole your business with the name.

tactics.name: Expand capacity with equipment, crews, and nearby territories
steps: Start with a post-hole digger and reinvest in a motorized auger to speed up jobs.
Add second and third crews and serve nearby cities if demand supports it.
Seek referral partnerships with handymen and landscapers.

tactics.name: Offer custom products that can be shipped
steps: Make, buy, or import distinctive mailbox designs rather than competing only on standard local installations.
Test products that are visually appealing and suited to photos and social sharing.
Use a storefront and targeted social ads to test demand for particular designs.

steps: Compare expected HOA job value with the extra effort required to win and deliver the contract.

warnings.warning: The host says not to place flyers inside mailboxes, describing it as illegal in the US. Check UK postal and direct-marketing rules before using a similar tactic.

Validate real willingness to pay before buying tools or formalizing the business. If direct prospects consistently prefer DIY or an existing handyman, the host recommends moving on or gathering a larger sample.
The host says jobs can involve insurance, unhappy customers, and free rework.
HOA contracts have longer sales cycles and can be difficult to manage.
The host warns that spreadsheet projections can look attractive while real operations remain difficult.
In the UK, follow PECR rules for unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals and sole traders; screen calls against TPS/CTPS where required.
Do not assume the host's gross-margin, conversion, demand, or market-size claims are independently verified.
The host promotes his own newsletter and podcast during the video, creating a promotional conflict.
